newsitem.title: UK: Israel aiding new West Bank settlements - Netanyahu.
newsitem.headline: Israel aiding new West Bank settlements - Netanyahu.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu acknowledged on Wednesday that his coalition was helping to expand Jewish communities in the occupied West Bank.
Speaking to BBC radio during a visit to London, Netanyahu was asked about a report on Israel's Channel Two television that his government had promised to build another 780 homes for Jews.
"We're helping with the infrastructure but we're not carting people in," Netanyahu, who is on the first leg of a European diplomatic tour, said.
"We're not in the process of building sectors. We build communities. Jewish communities grow naturally, the Arab communities in the West Bank grow and we're not hindering one or another," he said.
Senior Palestinian officials warned Israel on Saturday its expansion of Jewish settlements was leading Jews and Arabs towards "confrontation and disaster".
The television said Netanyahu made the promise on Sunday after the ultra-Orthodox Agudat Israel party threatened to leave his government unless more homes were built for religious Jews.
It said Netanyahu promised to approve another 580 housing units at Kiryat Sefer settlement and 200 more at Beitar settlement.
Palestinians want to establish an independent state in the West Bank and Gaza Strip with Arab East Jerusalem as its capital.
Interim peace deals the Palestinians cut with Israel's previous government, ousted by Netanyahu in May, gave them limited self-rule in parts of the territories.
Final status peace talks are to deal with these issues but have yet to resume under Netanyahu.
The Israeli prime minister reiterated his opposition to a Palestinian state but said he was determined to pursue talks with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.

"Things are difficult, I don't maintain that they're other than that. But I want to make it clear... this an orderly government. We are going to pursue peace, we're going to pursue the accords," Netanyahu said.
He said he envisaged a deal whereby the Palestinians would largely run their own affairs as a self-governing authority but with Israel responsible for security.
"It is possible to achieve it. It is not easy, and it is not pastel-coloured, but I am committed to move forward to a reality that will enable us to live in peace," Netanyahu said.

He was meeting opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair and former prime minister Margaret Thatcher on Wednesday before flying to Paris for talks with President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
